title: Post Completion Paralegal
company: The Eventus Recruitment Group - Agency - Permanent
description:
Eventus Legal are seeking a Post Completion Paralegal to join a dedicated post completion team in Spalding, Lincolnshire. This is a full-time, permanent, office based job offering a salary of £26,000 to £28,000 dependent on experience, private health insurance, an employer contributed pension and group life assurance. You will manage your own caseload of post completion files while reporting to a senior member of the property team.

Role Responsibilities

The Post Completion Paralegal in Spalding, Lincolnshire will take ownership of a varied caseload following completion of residential property transactions. Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing a caseload of post completion files from completion through to registration and closure
- Preparing and submitting Stamp Duty Land Tax returns and arranging payment where required
- Preparing, submitting and progressing applications to HM Land Registry
- Reviewing and responding to Land Registry requisitions within the relevant timescales
- Serving leasehold notices and dealing with certificates of compliance, restrictions and other title requirements
- Checking post completion documentation and maintaining accurate case management records
- Liaising with fee earners, lenders, managing agents, freeholders and other relevant parties to progress matters
- Closing files once all post completion requirements have been satisfied
- Reporting to a senior member of the property team and escalating complex issues appropriately

Person Specification

You will have practical experience of residential conveyancing post completion work and be comfortable managing competing deadlines. You should also be able to demonstrate the following:
- Experience managing a caseload of post completion files
- Knowledge of Stamp Duty Land Tax submissions and HM Land Registry applications
- An accurate and methodical approach to documents, records and deadlines
- Strong organisation and prioritisation skills
- Clear written and verbal communication skills
- The ability to work independently while contributing to a dedicated team
- Confidence using case management systems and standard Microsoft Office applications
- The ability to work full time from the firm's office in Spalding, Lincolnshire

Benefits and Rewards

This office based Post Completion Paralegal job in Spalding, Lincolnshire offers a competitive package and access to the firm's wider wellbeing benefits. The successful Post Completion Paralegal will also benefit from:
- A salary of £26,000 to £28,000 dependent on experience
- Free Parking
- Private health insurance for all employees
- Membership of the firm's personal pension plan with employer contributions of up to 4%
- Group life assurance of up to three times salary
- 25 days annual leave excluding bank holidays with the opportunity to buy and sell additional days
- Access to a 24-hour employee assistance programme and clinically trained mental health experts
- Access to trained Mental Health First Aiders
- Discounted legal fees following one year's employment
- Paid volunteering leave to support the local community
- Summer and Christmas social events
- Training, development and career progression opportunities

About the Law Firm

This extremely well established, multi-site regional law firm supports private individuals and businesses across a broad range of legal services. It offers a collaborative working culture, places training and development at the heart of its approach and provides opportunities for people to grow within the firm.

Next Steps

Apply now to be considered for this new Post Completion Paralegal opportunity in Spalding Lincolnshire. Alternatively, for a confidential discussion about this Post Completion Paralegal job, please send your CV to Izzie Vaughan at the Eventus Recruitment Group for a confidential discussion. Due to the high volume of applications, if you have not heard from us within ten days, unfortunately you have not been shortlisted on this occasion.

If this job isn't quite right for you but you are looking for a new position, please contact me at the details above for a confidential discussion on your career.

The Eventus Recruitment Group are award-winning recruitment specialists operating in the Legal, Finance and Financial Planning sectors across the UK. Please note, the years' experience and/or salary are listed in our advertisements as a guide. We are happy to consider applications from all candidates who are able to demonstrate the skills necessary to fulfil the role. As an equal opportunities employer we welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and circumstances. Our privacy policy can be found on the bottom of our website.

title: Community Administrator - Oasis Hub South Grimsby
description:
Community Administrator - Oasis Hub South Grimsby

Hours: 16 hours per week
Contract: 12 Month Fixed Term Contract (with potential extension subject to funding)
Salary: Grade F (£28,051 FTE, actual salary for 0.4 - 16 hours £11,220)
Location: Oasis Community Space, Nunsthorpe, Grimsby

Are you highly organised and passionate about supporting your local community?

Do you enjoy bringing order to busy projects while helping people stay connected and informed?

Want to use your administration, communication and digital skills to make a real difference?

At Oasis, our vision is for community: a place where everyone is included, making a contribution and reaching their God-given potential.

We are looking for a reliable and enthusiastic Community Administrator to join our team at Oasis South Grimsby. This role is central to ensuring the smooth running of our community work, supporting a wide range of projects, activities and events that positively impact children, young people and families across South Grimsby.

As our Community Administrator, you will provide essential administrative, financial and communications support to the local team. You will play a key role in maintaining accurate records, supporting reporting and monitoring processes, managing social media channels, and helping to communicate the impact of our work across the community

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is organised, proactive and enjoys working in a busy, people-focused environment where no two days are the same.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Community Leader and wider community team.
- Manage purchasing, stock orders, invoices and financial administration, ensuring records are accurate and up to date.
- Support monthly finance processes and maintain clear expenditure records.
- Maintain accurate project, attendance and outcome information on EVIDE and other monitoring systems.
- Produce reports, statistics and data summaries to support monitoring, evaluation and funding requirements.
- Create and manage engaging social media content promoting activities, events and community achievements.
- Design and produce promotional materials including posters, flyers, newsletters and digital graphics.
- Support community engagement through digital communications and respond appropriately to enquiries.
- Ensure all communications adhere to Oasis brand standards, safeguarding requirements and data protection regulations.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues, volunteers, schools and community partners.

The Successful Candidate Will Have
- Experience working in an administrative role and managing a varied workload.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Experience maintaining accurate records, including financial information.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications and shared filing systems.
- Experience using social media and digital communication platforms.
- The ability to analyse, manage and present data accurately.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- An understanding of confidentiality, GDPR and data protection principles.
- A commitment to safeguarding and the Oasis ethos of inclusion, equality, hope and perseverance.

It Would Be Great If You Also Had
- Experience working in a community, charity, education or youth setting.
- Experience using EVIDE or a similar CRM, beneficiary or impact-tracking system.
- Skills in creating promotional materials, photography, video editing or graphic design.
- Experience producing reports for funders or partner organisations.

As Part of the Package, Oasis Offers
- A pension scheme with a 7% employer contribution.
- A generous holiday allowance plus Bank Holidays.
- Ongoing training and development opportunities.
- Family-friendly policies and wellbeing support.
- The opportunity to be part of a national organisation committed to transforming communities.

To Apply please submit:
- Your CV
- A supporting statement (maximum two A4 pages)

Please use your supporting statement to explain how your experience, skills and personal qualities meet the requirements of the role.

Closing Date: 23rd October 2026
Interview Date: w/c 26th October 2026

We actively encourage applications from people of all ethnic backgrounds and underrepresented groups. If you require any assistance to overcome potential barriers during the recruitment process, please let us know.

We appreciate you may wish to use AI to support elements of your application, but we strongly encourage all candidates to submit applications that genuinely reflect their own skills, achievements and lived experiences. It is what makes your application stand out.

Oasis South Grimsby is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. All staff are expected to share this commitment. Appointment will be subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks, including an Enhanced DBS check.

The successful candidate must have the right to work in the UK. Oasis cannot assist with sponsorship or visa applications.

title: Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant
description:
Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant

Location: Caistor

Full Time

Monday to Friday 9:00am - 4:30pm

Manpower are currently recruiting for a Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant on behalf of our client. This is an excellent opportunity to join a well-established business where you'll play a key role in supporting payroll, accounts and administration functions within a close-knit and friendly team.

If you're an organised and detail-focused individual with payroll experience and a background in accounts support, we'd love to hear from you.

The Role

As a Payroll Clerk & Accounts Assistant, you'll be responsible for ensuring payroll is processed accurately and on time, whilst also providing support across the wider finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Process weekly and monthly payroll accurately and within deadlines
- Maintain and update employee payroll records
- Check timesheets, holiday records, sickness absence and payroll data
- Respond to payroll-related queries from employees
- Process new starters and leavers
- Assist with pension administration and payroll submissions
- Prepare payroll reports and maintain payroll documentation
- Process employee expenses
- Process purchase and sales invoices
- Support accounts payable and accounts receivable activities
- Assist with general office administration duties
- Provide additional support to the finance team as required

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous payroll experience (essential)
- Experience within an accounts or bookkeeping environment
- Strong understanding of payroll processes and confidentiality requirements
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Office applications
- Experience using Sage Payroll and Sage Accounts (desirable)
- Ability to work independently and manage competing deadlines
- Strong communication and problem-solving skills
- A professional, positive and team-focused attitude

What's in it for You?
- Competitive salary of £27,000 - £34,000, dependent on experience
- Monday to Friday working hours, 9:00am - 4:30pm
- Paid 30-minute lunch break
- 22 days annual leave, plus an additional day off for your birthday
- Extra time off over Christmas while working within a skeleton staff rota
- Early finish at 12:30pm every other Friday
- Join a supportive team of just three people, where your contribution will be highly valued
- Laptop provided for office use
- Free onsite parking

Apply Today

Apply now or contact the Manpower team for more information.

title: Emerging Talent and Resourcing Coordinator
description:
The Woodland Trust is looking for an Emerging Talent and Resourcing Coordinator to deliver an excellent recruitment experience and support our emerging talent programmes.

This role is advertised as full-time, 37.5 hours per week, however we would consider applications from those wanting reduced hours at 30 per week.

The Role:

Coordinate recruitment administration across the full hiring journey, from advertising vacancies and candidate communication through to onboarding and pre-employment checks.
Provide excellent customer service by responding to recruitment enquiries and supporting candidates, hiring managers and colleagues throughout the recruitment process.
Maintain accurate recruitment, candidate and vacancy records across people systems, ensuring compliance with GDPR and data protection requirements.
Produce and coordinate recruitment reporting, including candidate tracking, diversity data, purchase orders and invoice processing.
Build positive relationships with schools, colleges, universities and other external partners to support emerging talent initiatives.
Coordinate and attend careers fairs, open days and other engagement events, acting as a positive ambassador for the Woodland Trust and its apprenticeship programmes.
This is a hybrid position with a mix of home working and from our head office in Grantham, Lincolnshire. Head office attendance would be required once a month on average. Occasional travel to other offices and remote locations may also be required.
This is a fixed term contract until end of September 2027.

The Candidate:

Strong communication and organisational skills, with a keen eye for detail and a commitment to accuracy.
A customer-focused approach, with the ability to build positive relationships with candidates, hiring managers, new starters and external partners.
Confidence handling sensitive and confidential information with professionalism and discretion.
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, with experience managing and tracking programmes of work through large and detailed datasets.
Understanding of GDPR and data protection principles, particularly in relation to candidate and employee data.
Able to manage competing priorities, maintain high standards and work effectively within established processes.
Experience of working within a HR, People or recruitment environment would be advantageous.

Benefits and Wellbeing:

Joining our team means you'll be part of our fight for a greener, healthier planet for people and wildlife. We take good care of our staff, offering support and training opportunities. We also offer:

Enhanced Employer Pension
Life Assurance
Flexible and hybrid working options (7am - 7pm)
Generous annual leave - 25 Days plus Bank Holidays (pro rata for part-time)
Buy and sell holiday scheme
Enhanced parental pay
Employee assistance programme
To support inclusivity and remove barriers for candidates, we publish all salaries upfront and proudly follow the We Show the Salary pledge. The salary listed is the set salary for this role, and we don't ask applicants to state their current pay or expectations. If you choose to apply, we'll take that as confirmation that the advertised salary meets your expectations.

About Us:

The Woodland Trust is the UK's largest woodland conservation charity. We want to see a world where woods and trees thrive for people and nature. The Trust engages and inspires people to make a difference by protecting, restoring and creating woodland and getting more trees in the ground.

Our commitment to Diversity and Inclusion:

To achieve our mission, we need to better reflect society and the communities we work in. People of colour and disabled people are currently under-represented across the environment and conservation sector. If you identify as a person of colour and/or disabled, we particularly encourage you to apply.

Application information and advice:

For fairness we keep our candidates' personal details hidden from the hiring managers, and we do not ask for your CV at application.

Make sure that you answer the application questions to show your relevant skills and passion for the role. Even if you don't meet every requirement of the role, we encourage you to apply.

Completed applications will be reviewed by a hiring manager and/or a member of the recruitment team, and you will receive an update on the outcome of your application via email.

Acceptable Use - Artificial Intelligence (AI):

We understand that candidates may choose to use AI tools to support their job applications. However, we ask that any information submitted reflects your own experience, skills and understanding. During interviews, candidates are expected to respond independently without the use of AI tools.

Apply now:

If you're ready to make a difference and grow with us, apply today. We might close advertising early if we get a lot of applications, so it's a good idea to apply soon. If we do close the advert early, and you have an application in progress, we will email you prior to closing to give you time to complete.

Interviews will take place via MS Team, week commencing October 5th Interview questions will be provided before the interview to help you prepare.

title: Team Administrator
description: Due to expansion, a rewarding opportunity has arisen where we are looking for a reliable, organised and enthusiastic person with a strong work ethic to join our committed administration team in Children & Young People (CYP) Services for 37.5 hours per week working at the new Millenium Lodge Secure Children's Home on the outskirts of Sleaford. You will have a strong work ethic and be a key member of a friendly developing administration team providing a high standard of administration support and participating in service development and user care. You will also be responsible for contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the office to include referral processing, typing and formatting of correspondence, and other data requirements using clinical systems, Word, Excel, and Microsoft teams. There will be a requirement for note taking and other requirements of supporting a meeting. Due to the UKVI immigration changes we are no longer able to offer sponsorship for this role. Please provide details of the visa type and expiry date in your application. Failure to provide the required information will result in your application being rejected. To undertake secretarial administration duties in support of clinical and non-clinical activity in the CYP Service ensuring administrative support is available to management and members of the team as appropriate. This will include, but is not limited to: Inputting referrals and data onto the clinical system. Navigating and updating clinical systems and electronic databases. Gathering information. Help support with any rota coordination Typing/formatting letters and correspondence using audio/copy typing and word processing systems. Diary management. Help to assist with data monitoring using excel and Power BI housekeeping reports. The role would suit someone who enjoys working in a productive environment, takes pride in delivering high-quality administration and is keen to develop their skills within the service. You will be dealing with a wide range of tasks in a welcoming yet professional and sensitive manner ensuring confidentiality at all times. We will offer training and development opportunities for the successful applicant. There could be an expectation to travel to attend training or provide cover and mileage will be paid at a standard business rate. Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification documents for complete details regarding this post. When completing your application, please demonstrate how you meet the role criteria. We can also offer you many staff benefits to help support you which include: Early access to Psychological Therapies and Physiotherapy Competitive annual leave allowance Car leasing scheme NHS pension scheme Free eye tests Money saving options through our salary sacrifice scheme Discounts on major high street retailers and restaurants Please note, interviews for this vacancy are on 18th December 2025

title: Administrator
description: This is an exciting opportunity to join an established Lincolnshire Talking Therapy service as a B2 Administrative Assistant for the Skegness LTT Team. We are looking for an organised, flexible, efficient team player to join our busy mental health talking therapies service. The successful applicant will be based at Holly Lodge, Skegness, supporting service delivery, working Mon- Friday. The service will provide regular supervision and training to support this. You will require excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, as well as having an exemplary telephone manner, with the initiative to work on your own at times. Lincolnshire Talking Therapies is a successful service that provides a stepped care model for the treatment of people with mild to moderate mental health problems. For further information please contact Pamela Dennis, Team Manager, Skegness LTT via email at Pamela.dennis6@nhs.net We are not able to offer sponsorship for this role. Please provide details of the visa type and expiry date in your application. Failure to provide the required information will result in your application being rejected. As an Administrator, you will play a crucial role in supporting the smooth operation of our talking therapies service. You'll assist both clinical and non-clinical teams, ensure a welcoming environment for all visitors, and develop essential skills for a future NHS career. To undertake reception and routine administration duties in support of clinical and non-clinical activity, ensuring a professional and efficient reception service is provided for all visitors, including service users, carers, contractors, external and internal stakeholders, along with site colleagues and teams. Main Duties of the Apprentice Administrator (Mental Health NHS Talking Therapies): - Provide administrative support to the talking therapies team, including answering phones and responding to emails. - Assist with booking appointments, managing waiting lists, and scheduling assessments. - Maintain accurate and confidential patient records in line with NHS policies. - Welcome and guide service users, families, and visitors to the service. - Support the preparation and distribution of clinical documents, letters, and reports. - Help to organise meetings and take minutes when required. - Input data and generate routine reports for the team. - Work closely with clinical and administrative colleagues to ensure the smooth running of the service. - Uphold patient confidentiality and treat all information sensitively. - Undertake general office tasks such as photocopying, scanning, and filling Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details regarding this position.

title: Receptionist
description: The GP receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The core responsibilities of the receptionist are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record We currently have 2 part time vacancies available allowing us to be flexible for the right candidate. All hours will be worked between 08:00 and 18:30, Monday to Friday
